section_summary: This section reproduces Japanese laws and policy statements on administration in China, military conduct, total-war mobilization, occupation of southern territories, and compulsory labor service. Introductory notes frame these texts as evidence of Japan’s wartime organization and control. The final page introduces national-security legislation continued in the next section.

people.name: Tsukasa Kato
people.role: Lieutenant Colonel and Chief of the Military Affairs Bureau of the War Office

subfiles.title: Law for the Establishment of the Asia Development Council
subfiles.about: Establishes an advisory council for the Asia Development Board.
subfiles.summary: Sets out the council’s duties, membership, leadership and secretariat.

subfiles.title: Law for the Establishment of the Liaison Offices of the Asia Development Board
subfiles.about: Creates liaison bureaus for the Asia Development Board in China.
subfiles.summary: Defines bureau locations, staffing, supervision, branch offices and obligations to military commanders.

subfiles.title: Military Organization and Doctrine: Introductory Note
subfiles.about: Introduces the Imperial Rescript and Field Service Code.
subfiles.summary: Highlights military ideology and limited provisions concerning civilians and property.

subfiles.title: Excerpts from “Imperial Rescript To The Soldiers and Sailors”
subfiles.about: States five principles of conduct for Japanese soldiers and sailors.
subfiles.summary: The rescript calls for loyalty, propriety, valor, faithfulness, righteousness and simplicity, with sincerity presented as essential to all five precepts.

subfiles.title: Field Service Code of Japan
subfiles.about: Prescribes the beliefs and conduct expected of Japanese troops in the field.
subfiles.summary: The code stresses imperial loyalty, discipline, unity, aggression, victory, piety and self-sacrifice. Its field-service rules address military secrecy, propaganda, requisitioning and protection of enemy property and civilians. It also directs soldiers to maintain health, care for equipment, avoid excesses and preserve the army’s reputation.

subfiles.title: Official Statements of Policy on National Mobilization and the Administration of Occupied Areas: Introductory Note
subfiles.about: Introduces statements on total-war mobilization and southern occupation policy.
subfiles.summary: Identifies the Army Handbook and Kato’s statement as key policy sources.

subfiles.title: The Japanese Army’s Plan of Mobilization for Total War
subfiles.about: Outlines preparations to mobilize the whole nation for war.
subfiles.summary: Calls for peacetime preparation of ideology, education, industry, resources and finance, including taxation and government bonds.

subfiles.title: Japan’s Basic Policy for Administration of the Southern Territories
subfiles.about: Explains Japanese military, civil and economic policy for occupied southern territories.
subfiles.summary: Kato describes military oversight with civilian administration and selective use of existing local institutions. He addresses local customs, religion, Chinese merchants, Japanese settlers, language instruction and the obligations imposed on inhabitants. Economic sections prioritize strategic resources, especially oil, and discuss industrial selection, military currency, the Southern Development Bank, transport and economic pressure on Britain and the United States.

subfiles.title: Organization of the National Economy for War: Introductory Note
subfiles.about: Introduces the National Mobilization Law and National Service Requisition Ordinance.
subfiles.summary: Describes expanded wartime controls over labor, capital, industry and commodities.

subfiles.title: National Mobilization Law of Japan
subfiles.about: Authorizes comprehensive state control of people, goods, enterprises and information for wartime mobilization.
subfiles.summary: The law defines mobilization goods and businesses and grants the government powers over labor, trade, production, property, finance, prices, publications and business organization. It provides for requisition, expropriation, compensation, inspection and subsidies. Later articles prescribe penalties for violations, bribery and disclosure of secrets, and establish a mobilization commission.

subfiles.title: National Service Requisition Ordinance of Japan
subfiles.about: Sets procedures for compulsory assignment of Japanese subjects to mobilization work.
subfiles.summary: The ordinance specifies when workers may be requisitioned, how orders are issued and changed, and how fitness, wages and travel expenses are handled. It lists exempt categories and assigns duties to ministers, prefectural governors and local officials. Its territorial provisions extend the system to Korea, Taiwan, Karafuto and the South Seas Mandate.

subfiles.title: National Security: Introductory Note
subfiles.about: Introduces Japanese laws concerning political dissent and state secrets.
subfiles.summary: Describes peace-preservation legislation, thought control and the broad scope of defense secrecy.
